questions.prompt: Name a prophet explicitly mentioned in the Qur'an.

answers.explanation: The first human being and the first prophet. Allah taught him the names of all things.
Described in the Qur'an as "a man of truth and a prophet" whom Allah raised to a high station.
Called his people to Allah for 950 years before the great flood.
Sent to the ancient people of 'Ad, calling them to worship Allah alone.
Sent to the people of Thamud, with a she-camel from Allah as a sign.
Called Khalil — the intimate friend of Allah. He raised the foundations of the Ka'bah with his son Ismail.
Believed in Ibrahim's message and warned his own people against their wrongdoing.
Son of Ibrahim, praised in the Qur'an as "true to his promise". He helped build the Ka'bah.
Son of Ibrahim, given as good tidings to Ibrahim and his wife in their old age.
Son of Ishaq and father of Yusuf. On his deathbed he asked his sons whom they would worship after him.
His story — from the bottom of a well to trusted office in Egypt — fills an entire surah.
The Qur'an's great example of patience through illness and loss: "Indeed, We found him patient."
Sent to the people of Madyan, urging them to give full and honest measure and weight.
Allah spoke to him directly. He is the prophet named most often in the Qur'an.
Brother of Musa, appointed to strengthen and support him in his mission.
Named among the patient and the righteous — the Qur'an tells us very little else about him.
Given the Zabur (Psalms). The mountains and the birds joined him in glorifying Allah.
Taught the speech of birds and given command over the wind and the jinn.
Called his people away from worshipping the idol Ba'l.
Mentioned twice in the Qur'an, counted among the chosen and the best.
Swallowed by a great fish, he called out: "There is no deity except You; exalted are You."
Guardian of Maryam, who was granted a son, Yahya, in his old age.
Son of Zakariyya — the Qur'an notes that no one before him had been given that name.
Born miraculously to Maryam and given the Injil (Gospel).
The final messenger — the Qur'an calls him the "Seal of the Prophets".

"Do they not see the birds above them, spreading and folding their wings?"

Mules are mentioned alongside horses and donkeys as created for riding.
Allah is not shy to use the example of a mosquito, or what is even smaller.

Lice were one of the signs sent upon Pharaoh's people.
Bani Isra'il were given manna and quails as provision in the wilderness.
On the Day of Judgement people will be "like moths, scattered about".
A small creature of the earth ate away Sulayman's staff, revealing that he had died. It is commonly understood to be a termite.
